Glue — grammar

directional complements

Template: V + shànglai / xiàlai / chūlai / huíqù / guòqù / qǐlai

motion toward or away from the speaker — come up, come down, come out, go back, go over, get up

Ná chūlai kàn kan.
Tā pǎo shànglai le.

Foreigner traps

  • lái/qù is about where the SPEAKER stands, not who moves: bring it here = lái, send it there = qù.
  • Casual speech fuses and lightens the pair: ná chūlai → náchulai — the second half goes toneless.
  • shàng/qǐ/xià pick the landmark's geometry (up onto, up from, down off) — the ground decides, not politeness.

bǎ disposal

Template: bǎ + Object + V + result (complement, le, zài/gěi phrase)

"do something to/with the object" — the object moves or changes

Bǎ chuāng guān shang, tài lěng le.
Wǒ bǎ qián huán gěi tā le.

Foreigner traps

  • bǎ + bare verb is broken: bǎ shū kàn ✗ — something must HAPPEN to the object (wán, diào, shang, zài…, gěi…).
  • The object after bǎ is definite/known — nà běn shū is native, yì běn shū (some book) fights the frame.
  • Fate-verbs refuse bǎ: xǐhuan, zhīdào, rènshi can't be 'done to' an object — no bǎ nǐ xǐhuan, ever.

Recall quiz

Native notes — bǎ everywhere, the driver hail, and paying the bill

bǎ is the instruction-case

Warnings and requests live in bǎ: bǎ mén guān shang, bǎ dōngxi fàng hǎo — something gets handled, moved, changed. English speakers under-use it and sound like narrators; natives reach for bǎ the moment an object changes hands or place. Today's cards drill it with directionals — the two patterns weld together in real speech.

shīfu is the working address

Drivers, repairmen, movers, delivery: shīfu (master) respects the trade and never misses. shūshu (uncle) is for familiar older men, not service — calling a driver shūshu sounds charmingly lost. In a Chongqing cab the driver may answer you in dialect; your lēdiǎn from day 10 earns the fare-smile.

jié zhàng asks, mǎidān declares

jié zhàng is the neutral checkout hail — lǎobǎn, jié zhàng! Wǒ mǎidān steps up to pay for the table, and in Chongqing someone usually fights to say it first. The modern split is AA-zhì — wǒmen AA ba among peers — but expect the older script: the host pays, the guests protest, everyone wins.

zhēn shì trails into complaint

Tā zhēn shì… with the trailing pause does the eye-roll for you — finish with zǒng shì chídào or leave it hanging; the hanging version is the more withering. It's exasperation with affection, safe for friends, risky about bosses. zhēnshì written as one word is the texting form.
